title: Yitro: one person, one heart (Exodus 19:2)
hookLine: Rashi: at Sinai they camped like one person with one heart

lines: EVERYONE LOOKS AT THE SAME THING.
cards: A family road trip. Six hours of who's touching whom, which song, why we didn't stop at the last exit.
Then you arrive somewhere, the ocean maybe, or a canyon, and for one minute everyone in the car goes quiet and looks at the same thing. Nobody arranged it.

The Israelites have spent weeks arguing in the wilderness, about water, about food, about Moses. Now, in the third month after leaving Egypt, they come to the mountain. And one verb in the verse doesn't match the others.

teach.b: The verse says they set out from Rephidim, came to the wilderness of Sinai, and camped in the wilderness. Then it adds: and there Israel encamped before the mountain. In English, that sounds normal.
In Hebrew, the first verbs are plural: they journeyed, they came, they camped.

The last one switches to singular: vayichan, he camped. Israel camped as one. Rashi, the great eleventh-century commentator from France, following an older midrash, the Mekhilta, reads that switch on purpose.
Everywhere else, he says, they camped with complaints and quarrels.

Here they camped like one person, with one heart. Think who these people were: former slaves from different tribes, with different grudges, hungry, tired, frightened. Not one opinion, not one personality.
But for this moment, one heart, turned toward the same mountain. Notice what Rashi doesn't say. He doesn't say they agreed about everything.

It's a shared direction, a shared readiness. And the tradition ties this unity to what comes next: only a people camped like this, the commentators say, was ready to stand at Sinai and receive the Torah.
A tiny grammar shift, from they to he, and centuries of readers have heard in it the hope that people who disagree can still face the same way.

how: Rashi's phrase 'like one person with one heart' is often quoted in Jewish teaching about unity, especially around Shavuot, the festival of receiving the Torah at Sinai.

games.q: the verse says they journeyed, they came, they camped, and then: Israel camped. you're Rashi. what do you make of the singular verb?

only Moses camped; the people stayed back.
games.why: one person, one heart. everywhere else they camped in quarrels; here, for once, they faced the same way.

practice: Bring to mind someone you're often at odds with: a sibling, a coworker, a neighbor, someone across a political line.

You won't agree on everything, so look for one thing you both want, their kids safe, the project working, the parent you share cared for. Hold that shared mountain in mind, and if you pray, hold that person there too.
